title: Clinical Reserve Table: Fingerstick Reserve Strips in a Courtesy Reship
content:
A customer on insulin keeps a fingerstick reserve for sensor failures and warm-up periods, so a courtesy reship on the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program carries reserve strips according to the insulin regimen on the customer's open Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program.

| Insulin regimen recorded on the customer's open CGM program | Reserve strips |
|---|---|
| insulin pump | 40 |
| multiple daily injections | 30 |
| any other regimen, or no open CGM program | none |

**Rule.** To the strips a courtesy reship carries for its covered days and transit days are added, before they are divided into whole units, the reserve strips, which are 40 when the customer's open CGM program records the insulin regimen insulin pump, 30 when it records multiple daily injections, and none otherwise; an open CGM program is one that is not closed.

**Example (hypothetical).** A courtesy reship whose covered and transit days come to 44.4 strips for a customer whose CGM program on hold records multiple daily injections carries 74.4 strips, that is 1.49 units, rounded up to 2.
